title: Concurrent create with --userns=keep-id over the API sometimes produces a truncated ID mapping (start fails on ping_group_range)
body:
### Issue Description

When several containers with `--userns=keep-id` are created concurrently through the API service, one of them sometimes gets a truncated ID mapping that contains only the calling user. That container then fails to start, because container GID 0 is not mapped and crun cannot write the default sysctl `net.ipv4.ping_group_range=0 0` from `default_sysctls`:

```
Error: unable to start container "562e6076...": crun: write to `/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ping_group_range` (are all the IDs mapped in the user namespace?): Invalid argument: OCI runtime error
```

The mapping of the failed container versus its siblings created in the same batch:

```
kid-1 {"UidMap":["0:1:1000","1000:0:1","1001:1001:64536"],"GidMap":["0:1:1000","1000:0:1","1001:1001:64536"]}  started
kid-2 {"UidMap":["1000:0:1"],"GidMap":["1000:0:1"]}                                                             FAILED
kid-3 {"UidMap":["0:1:1000","1000:0:1","1001:1001:64536"],"GidMap":["0:1:1000","1000:0:1","1001:1001:64536"]}  started
```

In one earlier run a sibling that did start came out with `"1001:1001:195608"` as the last UID range instead of `64536`, with a GID range of `64536`, so the wrong value is not always the short form.

I found it through a compose tool that creates `deploy.replicas` containers concurrently over the REST API; about one `up` in four left a replica in `created`.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

With `podman.socket` running (rootless):

```sh
#!/bin/sh
P="podman --remote"
$P pull -q docker.io/library/alpine:latest >/dev/null
$P network create kidnet >/dev/null
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  $P rm -f -t 0 kid-1 kid-2 kid-3 >/dev/null 2>&1
  for n in 1 2 3; do
    $P create --name kid-$n --userns=keep-id --network kidnet docker.io/library/alpine:latest sleep infinity >/dev/null &
  done
  wait
  for n in 1 2 3; do
    printf 'cycle %s kid-%s %s ' "$i" "$n" "$($P inspect --format '{{json .HostConfig.IDMappings}}' kid-$n)"
    $P start kid-$n >/dev/null 2>/tmp/kid-err && echo started || { echo FAILED; cat /tmp/kid-err; }
  done
done
$P rm -f -t 0 kid-1 kid-2 kid-3 >/dev/null 2>&1
$P network rm kidnet >/dev/null
```

### Describe the results you received

3 of 60 containers failed in the last run (cycles 1 and 2), 7 of 30 and 3 of 30 in earlier runs. The failing container is always one with the `["1000:0:1"]`-only mapping.

What I varied, 30 containers each:

| Variant | Failed |
|---|---|
| `podman --remote`, user-created bridge network | 3, 3 and 7 of 30 across runs |
| `podman --remote`, default network | 0 of 30 |
| local `podman` (no service), user-created bridge network | 0 of 30 |
| local `podman` (no service), default network | 0 of 30 |
| `podman --remote run -d` one after another, bridge network | 0 of 30 (also 0 of 30 with `keep-id:uid=1000,gid=1000`) |
| parallel `create`, then `start` one after another | still fails (3 of 12 cycles) |

So it needs concurrent creates inside one service process; starting in series does not avoid it, creating in series does. The bridge network may only widen the window; I have not proven it is required.

### Describe the results you expected

Every container created with `--userns=keep-id` gets the same full mapping regardless of how many are created at once.

### podman info output

```
Client/server: 5.7.0 / 5.7.0
OCI runtime:   crun 1.21 (commit 10269840aa07fb7e6b7e1acff6198692d8ff5c88)
Distribution:  Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic
Rootless:      true, cgroups v2 with the systemd manager
Network:       netavark
/etc/subuid and /etc/subgid: <user>:100000:65536
Host /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ping_group_range: 0 2147483647
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

No

### Additional environment details

I have only reproduced this on 5.7.0, the version this distribution ships; I have not tried 6.1.2.

### Additional information

On my side I am working around it by creating `keep-id` containers one at a time.

comments.body:
Same truncation on podman 5.8.4 (Fedora 44, crun 1.28). Two things that may widen the issue:

**`keep-id` is not required.** A plain `docker run -d alpine sleep 30` over the socket, no `--userns` anywhere, already gets `["0:1:1000","1000:0:1","1001:1001:64536"]` for both maps — it is the default for rootless containers over the compat API. In my reproducer the one service that *did* declare `keep-id` started fine while six plain `alpine` services in the same batch got the truncated `["1000:0:1"]`.

**Second failure mode: `crun: mount 'devpts' to 'dev/pts': Invalid argument`.** The truncated map leaves no GID 5, and crun mounts `/dev/pts` with `gid=5` → EINVAL. Whether `ping_group_range` or devpts is the first casualty depends on the container. Noting it for discoverability: searching the devpts error does not lead here.

Evidence: 8 services in one `docker compose up -d`, 6 strand, 3 runs out of 3. I captured each generated OCI spec with a wrapper that copies `$bundle/config.json` before exec'ing crun — the specs differ only in `gidMappings`, the `/dev/pts` mount is byte-identical. One `cannot find UID/GID for user user: cannot read subids` debug line per container, including the successes; `getsubids -g user` is 60/60 under the same concurrency, so it is not the subid plumbing.

Workarounds, measured: one service per API call is 8/8 clean. `COMPOSE_PARALLEL_LIMIT=1` does **not** help — still 2 up, 6 stranded.
